Evidence/CLM-018
Evidence record

Institution-building steps are not evidence of operation or outcomes

What does this evidence establish?

Between June and August 2026, official records of the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden) show further institution-building in the payment system: integration work on the unified domestic money-transfer network, and the establishment and first governance steps of the Yemeni Payments and Clearing Company (YPCC), whose founding assembly was held on 3 August 2026. These are institutional steps; the operation and use of payment systems and any inclusion outcomes are separate evidence questions.

What does it measure?

Dated institutional and implementation steps in the payment system recorded by the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden) between 17 June and 4 August 2026.

Who or what does it apply to?

Institutions and events as stated in the source; not a population of users or transactions, and not a measure of system availability

When was it measured or observed?

2026-06-17 to 2026-08-04

How current is it?

The latest event in this record is the first board meeting of the Yemeni Payments and Clearing Company (YPCC) on 4 August 2026; the record covers 17 June to 4 August 2026. It should not be read as describing a later state unless a newer official record is published.

What this evidence does not establish

It does not show that the Yemeni Payments and Clearing Company (YPCC), the Fast Payment System (FPS) or the Real-Time Gross Settlement system (RTGS) is operating: YPCC is an institution that has been established, not a system in operation, and the results framework of the Financial Market Infrastructure and Inclusion Project (FMIIP) records FPS and RTGS as not yet developed or operational in January 2025, with no participating institutions; no later operational state is recorded here. It does not establish adoption, transaction coverage, reliability or any effect on financial inclusion.

Limits of the measure

The evidence records institutional and implementation states only; it contains no measure of participation, reliability, adoption or transaction coverage for these systems.
